title: Bose-Einstein condensates with Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling : An overview
abstract: Since their first realization more than a decade ago spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensates have been the subject of intense theoretical and experimental investigations. Spin-orbit coupling deeply modifies the equilibrium properties of the condensate, giving rise to novel configurations such as a supersolid stripe phase and a phase-separated plane-wave state. At the level of dynamics, both the frequency and the nature of the collective modes are significantly affected by the coupling with the spin degree of freedom. Here we review some of the most relevant advances in the field and provide our perspective on possible future research directions.
summary: This review surveys Bose-Einstein condensates with Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling, detailing how SOC modifies the system's equilibrium states. The work identifies three key phases—Stripe, Plane-Wave, and Single-Minimum—and outlines the phase transitions between them using mean-field theory. It is crucial for understanding superfluidity in spinor quantum gases.
main_problem: Reviewing the advances and future research directions concerning Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) subjected to Raman-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
main_result: The system exhibits distinct quantum phases—Stripe, Plane-Wave (PW), and Single-Minimum (SM)—whose transitions are controlled by tuning parameters like the Raman coupling strength ($\Omega_R$).
method: Theoretical analysis using the Gross-Pitaevskii mean-field approach to minimize the total energy functional.
model_or_system: The system is a BEC of ultra-cold atoms (e.g., $^{87}	ext{Rb}$) described by an effective spin-1/2 Hamiltonian incorporating SOC induced by Raman lasers. The dynamics are governed by a modified Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
key_observables: Density modulations (stripes), superfluid density ($ho_s$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi_M$), and the excitation spectrum (Bogoliubov modes).
important_parameters: Raman coupling strength ($\Omega_R$), interaction strengths ($g_{dd}, g_{ss}$), and average density ($ ar{n}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes equal intraspecies couplings ($g_{ds}=0$) and vanishing detuning ($\delta_R=0$). The system is treated in the mean-field limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single-particle spectrum, showing double-minimum structures, and depict the phase diagram mapping out the Stripe (I), Plane-Wave (II), and Single-Minimum (III) phases.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the theoretical framework starting from the single-particle Hamiltonian, derives the many-body mean-field energy functional, analyzes the resulting three distinct quantum phases based on parameter tuning, and discusses diagnostic tools like excitation spectra and susceptibility divergence.
why_interesting: It provides a comprehensive overview of how engineered spin-orbit coupling fundamentally alters the ground state structure (supersolid stripe phase) and dynamic excitations of BECs, which is central to modern AMO physics research.
